body:
329 of 572 files under tests/unit/ assert on production SOURCE TEXT (inspect.getsource,
Path.read_text, regex over a source file); 87 use inspect.getsource specifically.

Most of that is legitimate. Pinning the ABSENCE of a pattern, or the shape of a shell
script / workflow YAML / Dockerfile, is often the only way to check it at all.

The dangerous subset is narrower and worth naming: **a test whose assertion MESSAGE
promises a runtime behaviour or a causal mechanism, whose BODY only proves a string
exists, where the behaviour was executable all along.** It passes, it reads as coverage,
and it occupies the slot the real check would have taken.

## It is not hypothetical — one pinned claim is FALSE

tests/unit/test_kobo_admin_resend_book.py:81 asserts "ub.KoboSyncedBooks" appears in
do_kobo_resend, with the message:

    "without the deletion the next sync emits ChangedEntitlement rather than
     re-delivering the file."

cps/kobo.py:140 get_kobo_created_ts derives NewEntitlement vs ChangedEntitlement from
Books.timestamp / date_added ONLY. Deleting that row cannot change the entitlement type.
The same wrong belief is written into a production comment at cps/admin.py:1445 and into
the admin-visible success message at cps/admin.py:1461.

There IS an indirect path that makes resend appear to work, and it is why the belief
survived: cps/kobo.py:350 — if the user has NO remaining KoboSyncedBooks rows at all,
HandleSyncRequest resets the whole sync token, books_last_created included, to
datetime.min, and every book then arrives as NewEntitlement. So resend works when it
deletes the user's LAST row, which is the single-book case anyone would test by hand,
and does not work when any other synced row remains. Tracked separately as F-3e383a.

## The shape is convertible more often than it looks

Demonstrated in this branch. test_kobo_android_app_compat.py pins the string
"kobo.redirect_download_book" inside get_download_url_for_book with the message
"Android-device branch must route to the redirect_download_book endpoint". The branch
only reads request.headers — a Flask request context is enough:

    no header                 -> http://host:8083/kobo/TOK/download/7/kepub
    x-kobo-deviceos: Android  -> http://host:8083/kobo/TOK/redirect_download/7/kepub

tests/unit/test_kobo_android_download_url_executes.py now runs it. PROOF that this is
not cosmetic: changing endpoint_path from "redirect_download" to "download" in the
Android branch — leaving the pinned identifier untouched — keeps the source-pinned test
GREEN and fails the executing ones (2 failed, 9 passed).

## Families worth converting next, in order

1. test_kobo_android_app_compat.py — DrmType, empty Series, Pascal-case {Width}/{Height}
   image templates. All reachable through the Flask test client; assert on the emitted
   JSON, not on cps/kobo.py's text.
2. test_kobo_fully_local_oauth_handshake.py — the oauth_host rewrite and the
   /oauth/.well-known/openid-configuration payload. Invoke Init with proxy off and read
   the response, rather than asserting keys appear in source.
3. test_kobo_admin_resend_book.py — replace the pinned causal claim with a real sync:
   two synced books, resend one, call HandleSyncRequest, assert which entitlement wrapper
   comes back. That test would have failed and the false comment would never have shipped.

## What stays honest as a source pin

Anything asserting an absence, and anything whose subject is a file CI executes but Python
cannot import — shell scripts, workflow YAML, Dockerfiles. Those are not the problem.

## The rule worth adopting

If a test's failure message names a behaviour, the test should produce that behaviour. If
it cannot, the message should describe what it actually checks — "do_kobo_resend must
reference KoboSyncedBooks" — so the green is not read as more than it is. A wrong message
is worse than no test, because it stops the check that would have caught the failure.
title: Source-pinned tests promise runtime behaviour they never execute, and at least one pinned claim is false
